newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CITIC Pac details management buyout deal.
newsitem.headline: CITIC Pac details management buyout deal.

text.p: The chairman of CITIC Pacific Ltd broke his silence on Wednesday over a controversial management buyout deal which he said had been initiated by the company's Beijing parent which wanted to take profits.

"When we started CITIC Hong Kong, CITIC Beijing invested approximately HK$230 million and its quite natural that they would like to take some profit at this moment," Larry Yung told a news conference following the company's results announcement.
"So they raised the possibility of selling down shares to take profit. We then followed up with a request for a management buy out," he added.

A management team led by Yung bought a total of 330 million CITIC Pacific shares at HK$33 per share in mid-January from China International Trust & Investment Corp Hong Kong (Holdings) Ltd (CITIC Hong Kong).
CITIC Hong Kong is the privately-held investment arm of Chinese state trading company China International Trust and Investment Corp (CITIC Beijing).
The deal was widely criticised by analysts for being too secretive and priced at too large a discount.
The shares soared to a high of HK$44.30 after the deal was announced on December 30.
Yung said the discount was about 13-14 percent from HK$38-39 price the stock was trading at in November when they first negotiated the deal.
"Given to the size of the deal which is well over HK$10 billion, we considered such a discount would be appropriate," he said.
The price represented about a price earnings multiple of 21 times at the time, he added.
Yung said the management buyout proposal was the best option open to the company.
"It is well known that management was responsible for building up the company to what it is today so if management is buying the shares, CITIC Beijing could relax," he said.
When asked whether the deal required the approval of the Chinese authorities, Yung said he was concerned only with the deal complying with Hong Kong law.
He said it was up to CITIC Beijing to sort out the question of Chinese regulatory approval.
The management buyout reduced CITIC Hong Kong's shareholding in CITIC Pacific to 26.45 percent from about 41.92 percent.
Yung said the relationship between CITIC Hong Kong and CITIC Pacific was not at all affected by the deal.
The management had no plan to sell out shares. They will hold them for long term investment purposes for at least two years, he said.
